A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, figures, Tables 1–14 and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3DSSG evaluations, component ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D, including a weakly supervised experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative analyses and weakly supervised experiment reported in v1.

M1.justification: The object encoder, contrastive objectives, relationship encoder, LSE, GSE and BEG procedures in Sections 3.1–3.4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3DSSG indoor-scene data and SGCls/PredCls tasks, including the same seen/unseen-triplet evaluations in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments: SGPN, SGFN, VL-SAT and Zhang et al. remain in their comparisons, as do KERN in Table 10 and 3D-VLAP in Table 14.

E3.justification: The data split, preprocessing, training budgets, recall metrics, graph constraints and fully/weakly supervised settings are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C–D.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component, loss, modality, gating and relationship-input ablations, together with the entropy analysis, feature visualizations and scene-graph case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–14 contain identical numerical results. The empirical plots and qualitative examples are also unchanged; Figure 1's revised schematic illustrates the same existing contrast.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and method equations are unchanged, as are Appendix B's assumptions, Propositions 1–2, proofs and contrastive-loss derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about object discrimination, encoder transferability, spatial and directional components, and improved closed-vocabulary 3DSSG prediction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of object-feature quality and component interactions are unchanged. Both retain the same open-vocabulary qualifications and limitations concerning object detection and incremental graph updates.

D1.justification: The printed code link and Appendix C's software, hardware, preprocessing, hyperparameters, training times and checkpoint-selection information are identical.

R1.justification: The reference list and Appendix A's related-work discussion are unchanged, including the positioning relative to contrastive learning and alternative scene-graph approaches.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp is updated, and Figure 4 hyphenates 'Distance-based Attention.' The narrative prose and section/appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 are restyled. Figure 1 adds shaded embedding clusters and stronger node/edge highlighting; Figure 4 changes label rendering, with some mathematical symbols becoming less legible. Captions, table structures and figure placement are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 1 gains clearer grouping and highlighting, but Figure 4 renders the previously legible g_ij label as a diamond-like symbol and makes refined-feature labels harder to read. These defects reduce the architecture diagram's technical clarity. With the scientific content unchanged, this limited regression outweighs the modest visual gain.
